clue.text: How much of the main substance is present? It's madness to include lithium

definitions.text: How much of the main substance is present?

indicators.note: to include means to hold within, so the chemical symbol is placed inside the other word

parts.note: madness is insanity, which Paul reads as 'in sanity': the lithium goes in the word for a sound mind
LI is the chemical symbol for lithium

explanation.surface: Lithium treats madness, so including it sounds sensible, set beside a question about how much salt is in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the sea, so its substance is salt. Insanity read as 'in sanity' tells you where LI goes: inside SANITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Salinity measures the saltiness of water, how much salt the sea holds.

clue.text: Miss the captain

definitions.meaning: to miss something, such as a class, is to fail to attend it or leave it out
the captain of a curling or bowls team is called this, a short form of skipper

explanation.surface: Someone decides not to see the captain, or misses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: to omit or pass over, and a team's leader, informally short for skipper.

clue.text: Cut rail route from Birmingham?

indicators.note: said in a Brummie accent, from Birmingham, the vowel of the word for a railway route comes out as 'oi'

parts.note: a railway route is a line

explanation.surface: A question about a railway route leaving Birmingham being axed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Birmingham (Brummie) accent famously turns the 'i' of LINE into an 'oi' sound. 'Cut' looks like a verb about closing the route, but it is the definition: a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher's cut of meat from the back of the animal, between ribs and hips.

clue.text: Mobile phone rings zero — futile

indicators.note: rings means surrounds, so the anagram goes around the letter for zero
mobile means moving about, so the letters of the next word are shifted around

parts.note: zero is the round letter O

explanation.surface: Someone's mobile phone keeps ringing with nobody there, and it all seems pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile' turns PHONE into NHOPE; 'rings' puts O inside it after the N.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation with no chance of success is hopeless; the idiom describes something futile.

clue.text: A game of two halves?

parts.note: the football cliché 'a game of two halves', read literally: two halves add up to a total, so a full game is a total of football

explanation.surface: The old football commentator's cliché about a match of two halves.
explanation.walkthrough: Two halves make a whole, the total. Total football is also a real style of play, made famous by the Dutch in the 1970s, where any outfield player can take any position.
explanation.definitionFit: Two halves add up to the whole match, the sum of the football, and that is also the name of a famous fluid playing system.

clue.text: A run of four points ending in poor return

parts.note: the four points of the compass in a row: north, south, west, east

indicators.note: ending in picks out the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A batsman scores four runs but ends up with a poor return.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture (a run, a four, a poor return) is false: the four points are the compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A return can be a reply, as in a quick retort, so the noun meaning a reply fits.

clue.text: Tripping in a tango, why does this keep happening?

indicators.note: tripping means stumbling, so the letters of the dance phrase fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A dancer keeps stumbling during the tango and despairs at the repeated mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tripping' makes the letters of IN A TANGO stumble into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: The exasperated exclamation at a recurring mishap is the same feeling as asking why it keeps happening.

clue.text: In site of caves, whisper sweet nothings through the door?

parts.note: to whisper sweet nothings is to court someone, to woo
a way of speaking through a closed door is via its keyhole

explanation.surface: A lover whispering endearments through a door, set somewhere among caves.
explanation.walkthrough: Wookey Hole is a show cave in Somerset, in south-west England. The picture is a suitor courting through a keyhole.
explanation.definitionFit: A village in Somerset famous for its show caves, a well-known tourist site.

clue.text: Regarding something to sign, regarding something to sign?

parts.note: regarding means about, which is the short word RE
a petition is a document people sign to show support

explanation.surface: A memo subject line accidentally typed twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of the clue gives the wordplay; the second half, the same words again, is the definition, since the clue repeats itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the same words a second time is the very thing named, and the clue does it in front of the solver.

clue.text: Girl needs way to cut chop for traditional dish

parts.note: Iris is a girl's name

indicators.note: to cut means to slice into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to hew is to chop, as with an axe
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A girl must find a way to cut up a chop to make a traditional dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chop' reads as a cut of meat for the stew, but it is the verb to hew.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutton or lamb stew with potatoes and onions, the classic national dish of Ireland.

clue.text: Make any saddo a drink?

parts.note: read in two parts, the answer is WHISK, a word for mixing, followed by a jumble of the letters A N Y S A D D O, so it tells you to mix up 'any saddo'

explanation.surface: Pour any sad loser a drink to cheer them up.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as WHISK + YANDSODA: whisk means mix, and YANDSODA is ANYSADDO jumbled. So the answer itself says 'mix any saddo', which is what the clue asks.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch topped up with fizzy water is a classic mixed drink.

clue.text: Company having bad time in recession

indicators.note: in recession means going backwards, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: bad can mean poor in quality

explanation.surface: A firm struggling through a hard time in an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' turns POORT backwards. 'Company' looks like a business, which fits the recession, but here it means a body of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A military company or unit of soldiers; troop and company are both army groups.

clue.text: Hogwarts' English exam?

parts.note: an English exam checks the correct writing of words; at Hogwarts, the wizarding school in the Harry Potter books, a test of magic would be one too

explanation.surface: An English paper sat at the school of wizardry.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the second sense of a spell: a word's written form, and a magical incantation.
explanation.definitionFit: A classroom quiz on writing words correctly; at a school of magic it would test charms.

clue.text: Muslim ruler who's unwise, did you say, to get fast food item?

parts.note: thick means slow-witted, unwise

indicators.note: did you say signals that the word for the ruler is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a sheikh is an Arab or Muslim leader

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a foolish Muslim ruler being given fast food.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer swaps the order: THICK comes first, then SHAKE, which sounds like 'sheikh'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense milkshake sold at burger chains, a fast food item.

clue.text: Overly concerned about cost, I twice put off retiring

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps the rest

parts.note: anal, informally, means fussily over-concerned with detail

indicators.note: put off means disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order
twice means the letter is used two times

explanation.surface: A penny-pincher keeps postponing retirement, being overly worried about cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' jumbles COST, I and I into TISOCI. 'retiring' is shy, not stopping work.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone retiring shuns company, and an unsociable, reclusive person avoids others.

clue.text: Suspicion of faith, in truth

indicators.note: of here means taken from, so the letters come from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A question of whether one's faith is truly sincere.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across faitH IN Truth, so the word 'in' gives up its letters rather than acting as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspicion of something is a slight trace of it, a faint suggestion.

clue.text: Story going over one's head?

parts.note: a story is a lie; pork pie, short for porky pie, is rhyming slang for a lie
a hat is something that goes over the head

explanation.surface: A tale too clever for the listener, going over their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porky pies' is cockney rhyming slang for lies, so a story (a fib) is a pork pie. The whole clue also describes the hat: something named after a story that sits over one's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-crowned felt hat shaped like the pie, worn over the head.

clue.text: Coventry City, the depression of the sports broadcasters?

parts.note: Sky is the British satellite TV company famous for its sports channels
the blues are a fit of depression

explanation.surface: A football club's gloom shared with the TV companies that cover the game.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sky Blues is the nickname of Coventry City, an English football club, from its pale blue kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Coventry City's nickname, taken from the light blue of their shirts.

clue.text: Mammal after insect, one of these oiled

indicators.note: after means following, so the mammal is placed behind the insect

parts.note: a cricket is a chirping insect
a bat is a flying mammal

explanation.surface: A mammal chasing an insect, which some creature then oils.
explanation.walkthrough: A new willow bat is treated with linseed oil to protect it, hence 'oiled'.
explanation.definitionFit: A willow cricket bat is traditionally rubbed with linseed oil to stop it drying and cracking.

clue.text: Composer has no limits for voice

indicators.note: having no limits means losing its outer edges, so the first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: Sir William Walton was an English composer

explanation.surface: A composer with boundless range writes for the voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no limits' drops the first and last letters of WALTON.
explanation.definitionFit: A singing voice, the lowest female or highest adult male range in a choir.

clue.text: Wrong exposition in New York?

parts.note: the United Nations, UN, is headquartered in New York
an exposition is a show or trade fair

explanation.surface: An exhibition held in New York goes awry.
explanation.walkthrough: The United Nations has its headquarters in New York, so a show held there could be called a UN fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Unjust or wrong treatment is not just, the adjective for something not right.

clue.text: Heading for Sydney, the plane's ready for you, sport!

indicators.note: heading here means the start, so the first letter of the city name is taken

parts.note: the airport announcement that a flight is ready means passengers are being called to get on now

explanation.surface: An airport announcement calling a passenger onto a flight to Sydney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading for' looks like travel towards Sydney, but it takes the city's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A winter sport of sliding down snowy slopes on a single wide board.

clue.text: Secure business

definitions.meaning: secure means stable and fixed, not wobbly

explanation.surface: A safe company.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: solid or steady as an adjective, and a company as a noun.

clue.text: Certainly, you will need a hospital

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone assures you that you'll certainly need hospital treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal yes, used to agree or affirm, much like saying certainly.

clue.text: Last word in gold, something cast in it

indicators.note: in it means placed inside the previous thing, the gold

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is cast in dice games

explanation.surface: The final word on gold, something poured in a mould.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests metal poured into a mould, to go with gold, but a die is cast in a game of dice.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell is the last thing said on parting, the French goodbye.

clue.text: Double I, double K, double O, double L, a different E

indicators.note: different signals that all these letters go into another order
double means the letter is written twice
double means this letter too appears two times
double again means two copies of the letter

explanation.surface: A list of doubled letters, like spelling something aloud, with a stray E.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'Double' is the definition; the others double K, O and L. 'different' rearranges I, KK, OO, LL and A into LOOKALIK, with E kept at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is a person who looks just like someone else, a twin or dead ringer.

clue.text: Join up lines around triangle at first

indicators.note: around means scattered about, so the letters are moved into a new order
at first means only the opening letter of the shape is taken

explanation.surface: Instructions for joining lines round a triangle in a geometry lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal; here it rearranges LINES plus T, the first letter of triangle.
explanation.definitionFit: To join up is to sign on for military service, to enrol in the forces.

clue.text: Natural boxer cut on the bottom beginning to hurt, giving grunt

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: hares naturally box, standing up and sparring, in spring
the rump is the backside, the bottom

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A boxer takes a low blow and grunts in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Natural boxer' suggests a gifted fighter, but it is an animal: hares box in spring. 'cut' takes the E off HARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gruff throat-clearing noise of disapproval, the kind of grunt a stuffy person gives.
